lines: The Central Bank limit for a first-time buyer is 4 times gross income: €400,000 on €100,000 (both incomes). Lenders decide within it, and may lend above it only under the 15% allowance.
Within the Central Bank limits, up to €444,000 with a €44,400 deposit over 30 years; lenders decide.
For a €400,000 home: a €360,000 mortgage (90% of the price) and a €40,000 deposit.
Needed at the keys: €47,000 (the deposit, €4,000 stamp duty and about €3,000 for legal fees and a survey).
At €1,000 a month from €30,000, that is saved around April 2028, before interest: by June 2028, the date given.
Help to Buy is not counted above: up to €35,000, it is limited by the Income Tax and DIRT paid over the last four tax years, not given.
Savings: the top rate on the market is 3.11% (bunq), about €736 interest after DIRT by June 2028 in that account; 28 accounts fit.
Mortgages: 51 fit €360,000 over 30 years, from €1,537 to €2,147 a month.

savings.basis: The highest rate on the market for money that can be reached by June 2028, among 28 accounts that take this saving; interest after DIRT; no product is picked.

mortgage.basis: Every lender’s mortgages that fit €360,000 at 90% of the price over 30 years for a first-time buyer, fixed and variable, one per lender, rate type and fixed period; the monthly repayment at each one’s initial rate; no lender is picked.

lines: Savings: the top rate on the market is 3.11% (bunq), about €736 interest after DIRT by June 2028 in that account; 28 accounts fit.
Mortgages: 51 fit €360,000 over 30 years, from €1,537 to €2,147 a month.

assumed: First-time buyer, as nothing else was said: the 4 times income limit applies (3.5 times for a second or later buyer).

routes.name: New build with Help to Buy
routes.mechanism: A tax refund from Revenue towards the deposit: 10% of the price, at most €35,000
conditions: A first-time buyer, in a new build bought from a builder or a self-build
A price (or self-build valuation) of €500,000 or less
A mortgage of at least 70% of the price
At most the Income Tax and DIRT paid over the last 4 tax years (not USC or PRSI)
Lived in as the main home for 5 years; bought or built by 2029-12-31

sources.fact: New builds (construction subject to VAT), self-builds and converted non-residential buildings; €500,000 or less
The lesser of €35,000 (applications from 7 October 2026), 10% of the price or valuation, and Income Tax and DIRT paid in the four years before applying; USC and PRSI not counted
A first-time buyer, living in it as their main home for five years; a mortgage of at least 70% of the price; bought or built by 31 December 2029

routes.line: New build with Help to Buy: keys Nov 2026 if your tax paid covers €35,000
routes.reason: Up to €35,000 Help to Buy is counted on this route only; it is limited by the Income Tax and DIRT paid over the last four tax years, which was not given.
routes.missing: How much Income Tax and DIRT was paid over the last four tax years?

routes.name: Second-hand
routes.mechanism: A mortgage within the Central Bank limits, with the deposit and buying costs saved
conditions: A mortgage of up to 4 times gross income (3.5 for a second or later buyer) and 90% of the price; lenders decide within it
Stamp duty of 1% and about €3,000 for legal fees and a survey (an estimate)
No Help to Buy: it is for new builds and self-builds

sources.fact: Loan-to-income 4 times (first-time buyers) and 3.5 times (second and subsequent); loan-to-value 90%; allowances 15% of each; framework reviewed October 2022, S.I. 546 of 2022 from 1 January 2023
Stamp duty of 1% on a home up to €1,000,000

routes.line: Second-hand: keys Apr 2028, €47,000 needed at the keys
routes.reason: For a €400,000 home: a €40,000 deposit, €4,000 stamp duty and about €3,000 in fees, before interest.

routes.name: Vacant property grant
routes.mechanism: A grant for works after purchase, paid on receipts; not deposit money
routes.line: Vacant property grant: up to €50,000 for works after purchase, not the deposit
routes.reason: Up to €50,000 (€70,000 if derelict) for a home vacant 2 years or more, paid after the works.
conditions: Vacant for at least 2 years
Built before 2008 (Limerick’s page; South Dublin’s says before 2007)
Up to €50,000, and up to €20,000 more if derelict
Paid on receipts after the approved works, finished within 18 months
To live in or to rent out; applied for through the council where the home is

sources.fact: Secondary to gov.ie (refused automated reads on 2026-11-10), from the council that administers it: up to €50,000, up to €20,000 more if derelict; vacant at least 2 years; built "before 2007"; paid on invoices and receipts after the approved works; works within 18 months; a home or a rental; may apply while negotiating to buy
Secondary to gov.ie, from the council: up to €50,000, up to €20,000 more if derelict; vacant at least two years; "built prior to 2008"; a permanent home or a rental

routes.name: First Home Scheme
routes.mechanism: Shared equity: the scheme funds part of a new home’s price and holds that share
conditions: A new build in a private development, a self-build, or buying the home rented after a notice to sell
First-time buyers or Fresh Start
Up to 30% of the price, 20% with Help to Buy; at least 2.5% or €10,000
Mortgage approval with a participating lender, borrowing the most it offers (up to 4 times income)
A 10% deposit; Help to Buy can count towards it
Price within the local ceiling (€375,000 to €500,000 by area)
Not with the Local Authority Home Loan or affordable purchase

sources.fact: First-time buyers, first-time self-builders and Fresh Start applicants; a new build in a private development, a self-build, or a tenant purchase; up to 30% of the price or build cost, 20% with Help to Buy; combinable with Help to Buy, not with the Local Authority Home Loan or affordable purchase

Over 18; mortgage approval with a participating lender, borrowing the most it offers (up to 4 times income); a 10% deposit; the share at least 2.5% or €10,000; the principal private residence; no household income limit
Price ceilings per local authority area, €375,000 to €500,000 (house, apartment, self-build); "regularly reviewed and may be subject to change"; no effective date on the page

routes.line: First Home Scheme: shared equity up to €80,000, if the ceiling allows
routes.missing: Which county is the home in?

routes.name: Local Authority Home Loan
routes.mechanism: An alternative mortgage from the council, up to 90% of the home’s value
conditions: Gross income at most €80,000 single, €85,000 joint
Proof of insufficient mortgage offers from 2 regulated lenders
A first-time buyer (Fresh Start and inherited property excepted)
Aged 18 to 70; two years’ employment (one for a second earner)
A market value within the county limit (€310,000 to €415,000)
Not with the First Home Scheme

sources.fact: Gross income at most €80,000 single, €85,000 joint; proof of insufficient offers from two regulated lenders; a first-time buyer (Fresh Start and inherited property excepted); aged 18 to 70; two years’ employment (main earner), one year (second earner)

Maximum market value: €415,000 Dublin, Kildare, Wicklow; €375,000 Cork, Galway City, Meath; €345,000 Clare, Galway County, Kilkenny, Limerick, Louth, Waterford, Westmeath, Wexford; €310,000 elsewhere (S.I. 701 of 2021 or later regulations; no effective date on the page)
Up to 90% of the market value; the maximum loan depends on where the property is; price and income limits raised from 1 April 2026

routes.line: Local Authority Home Loan: not at €100,000 joint income, the ceiling is €85,000
routes.reason: Gross income of €100,000 is above the €85,000 joint ceiling.

routes.name: Affordable purchase
routes.mechanism: A council home sold below market value; the council keeps the difference as its share (at least 5%)
conditions: Only homes a council advertises (listed as Starter Home Purchase); each advert has its own opening and closing dates
A first-time buyer or Fresh Start
Gross household income times 4 at most 85.5% of the home’s market value
The council keeps an equity share of at least 5%
Help to Buy can count towards it; the First Home Scheme cannot

sources.fact: Secondary to gov.ie (refused automated reads on 2026-11-10): the Department of Housing and Housing Agency site lists council affordable homes as Starter Home Purchase; the council sells a new home below market value and keeps the difference as its equity share

First-time buyer or Fresh Start; gross household income times 4 at most 85.5% of the market value; the council’s share at least 5%; Help to Buy can count (mortgage and share at least 70%); the First Home Scheme is not available for council homes; each home is advertised with its own opening and closing dates

routes.line: Affordable purchase: not at €100,000 income for a €400,000 home, the limit is €85,500

questions.question: Is this a first home (never owned one before)?
Fixed rate, variable, or show both?
What do you pay in rent a month? (optional)
